questions.q: In the modern Named Credentials model, what does an External Credential define?
options: The governor limit for callouts in a transaction
The callout endpoint URL only
The authentication protocol and one or more Principals holding the real authentication parameters
The Apex class that performs the callout
questions.explain: An External Credential defines how authentication works — its protocol and its Principals — separately from where the callout goes.

questions.q: What does a Named Credential store?
options: A list of governor limits for the org
The WSDL for a SOAP web service
A username and password directly
The callout endpoint URL, plus a reference to the External Credential that supplies authentication
questions.explain: A Named Credential points at an endpoint and references an External Credential for authentication — it never stores the password itself.

questions.q: What is the difference between a Named Principal and a Per-User Principal?
options: A Named Principal is one shared identity used by everyone with access; a Per-User Principal has each individual user supply their own credentials
There is no functional difference — the terms are interchangeable
A Per-User Principal is required for every External Credential, with no exceptions
A Named Principal is used only in SOAP callouts, while Per-User is used only in HTTP callouts
questions.explain: A Named Principal represents one shared system identity, common for system-to-system integration, while Per-User Principals let each user authenticate individually.

questions.q: What controls whether a given user's Apex transaction is allowed to actually use a configured Named Credential?
options: Whether the Apex class is marked global
A Permission Set that grants access to the External Credential's Principal
The org's API version
Whether a Remote Site Setting also exists for the same URL
questions.explain: Access to a Named Credential's Principal is granted through a Permission Set — without it, the callout fails on authentication even if the Apex code is correct.

questions.q: What does the Apex endpoint value `callout:My_Named_Credential/orders` actually do?
options: It bypasses the Permission Set access check for convenience
It fails immediately, since `callout:` is not valid Apex syntax
It tells the platform to resolve the real endpoint URL and inject the correct authentication at send time, without exposing the secret in code
It triggers a SOAP callout instead of an HTTP callout
questions.explain: The `callout:` prefix resolves to the Named Credential's real URL and auth headers at send time, keeping secrets out of the Apex code and debug logs — it does not bypass the permission check.
